title: Weekly Challenge: Live Industry Office Hours
hook: Students drop into a mentor's 30-minute office hours. Design the system that runs it live.
description: This week's challenge: design the backend for live industry "office hours." A mentor opens a 30-minute slot; any number of students can join, raise a hand, ask questions in a shared queue, and watch answers in real time. When the slot ends, a recap (questions asked + answers) is saved to the mentor's and students' records. Respect everyone's time: joining should take seconds, and a student who arrives late should instantly see the current state.
constraints: Up to 500 students may join a single session; ~50 concurrent across the platform.
Question queue and answers must update in near real time (< 2s).
A late joiner must load the full current state (queue + answered) on connect.
Recap must persist after the session ends; sessions are ephemeral but recaps are durable.

title: Peer Demo Feedback in Under a Minute
hook: A student posts a 2-minute demo. Peers leave quick, structured feedback. Design the pipeline.
description: Design a system where students post short project demos (video link + blurb) and peers leave structured feedback in under a minute (a few tags + one sentence). The feature must "solve the empty room": a brand-new demo should still surface to a few relevant peers so it doesn't sit with zero responses. Feedback becomes part of the author's visible record.
constraints: Submitting feedback should take a peer under 60 seconds.
A new demo must be routed to at least a few potential reviewers automatically.
Feedback is public and attributed; it aggregates onto the author's profile.
Spam/low-effort feedback should be cheap to filter out later (keep the shape structured).
